about: Capstone C0, Behind one meter (wave W3, 2026-11-03): the note's fields, the exemplars and the rubric's look-for lines. The plan runs on engine E0 (assets/learn/components/engine-e0.js, data e0.json), the Site Bench's engine. The exemplars are illustrative notes about the default plan (the Prairie Town home with 6 kW of rooftop solar); every number in them is the engine's, checked by _tests/learn/test_c0-behind-one-meter.js.

note.title: Your one-page note
note.lede: Write three short parts in your own words; the plan, its results, the assumptions, the sensitivity line and the limits fill in from your last run.

fields.label: Recommendation
fields.hint: Two sentences: what this site should install, or not, and the number that decides it.

fields.label: What the site cannot do alone
fields.hint: One or two sentences: what it still needs from the grid or a buyer, and when.

fields.label: What would change the answer
fields.hint: One sentence from your sensitivity chart: which input, and how far it would have to move.

exemplars.title: Two notes on the same plan
exemplars.lede: Both recommend about the default plan: the Prairie Town home with 6 kW of rooftop solar. Tap a numbered phrase.
exemplars.task: Should the Prairie Town home install 6 kW of rooftop solar?

parts.note: A saving without its cost: the panels cost $28,430 up front, and the [[net-present-value|NPV]] over 25 years is −$17,813.

parts.text: solar is clean, so the home goes green
parts.note: No number and no boundary: operating CO₂ falls from 5.9 t to 3.1 t a year, with grid power at one average factor.

parts.text: With a battery it could leave the grid.
parts.note: A claim the bench never tested: the home still buys from the grid in 5,240 hours a year.

parts.text: Do not buy 6 kW of solar at the sourced costs: its NPV over 25 years is −$17,813 at 4% real
parts.note: The decision first, with the number that decides it, its horizon and its rate.

parts.text: It cuts the home's operating CO₂ from 5.9 t to 3.1 t a year (Kansas's average grid factor).
parts.note: CO₂ with its size and its boundary.

parts.text: The home still needs the grid in 5,240 hours a year, every night.
parts.note: What the site cannot do alone, in the bench's own numbers.

parts.text: At 75% of the equipment cost the NPV is still −$10,237; an 8¢ export credit gives −$14,717.
parts.note: The sensitivity test that could have changed the answer, and did not.

diff.label: Decision
diff.good: Do not install yet, because the NPV is negative

diff.label: Numbers
diff.good: NPV, saving, CO₂ and grid hours, each with its unit

diff.label: Sensitivity
diff.good: The two inputs most likely to flip the answer

exemplars.note: Both notes are illustrative; their numbers are the bench's for the default plan.

rubric.title: Rate your note against the course rubric
rubric.lede: Pick the level your note reaches on each of the four competences this capstone builds.

competences.look: NPV and CO₂ for the same plan, against the same site with nothing new, in one dollar year, with the CO₂ boundary said.
A sensitivity chart of the NPV with the plan held fixed, and the input that matters most named with its range.
What the site still needs from outside (the grid, a buyer) and what the bench leaves out (outages, storage across weeks).
A page an owner can act on: the recommendation first, then the numbers that back it.

rubric.note: Proficient on all four is the bar for this capstone.

sensitivity.title: Test the plan: what moves its NPV?
sensitivity.lede: Each bar swings one input while the plan stays fixed. Equipment cost and the rate need no new run; a price is run again through all 52 weeks.
